candidates.source_title: Rochdale’s Kenion Street album brings local artists to national radio
candidates.source_summary: An album featuring local artists’ versions of songs recorded in Rochdale has received national radio airplay following its release this summer.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An album featuring local artists’ versions of songs recorded in Rochdale has received national radio airplay following its release this summer. Kenion Street features 11 tracks originally recorded at Cargo or Suite Sixteen studios, performed by acts from the borough. Released on vinyl and digital platforms as part of Rochdale’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture, the album includes PoolEra’s version of OMD’s Electricity, Medley performing New Order’s Dreams Never End and Jennifer Read covering The Fall’s Totally Wired. The recordings were produced by Jamie Alsop at Voltalab Sound Studios, which occupies the original Cargo and Suite Sixteen building on Kenion Street. Between 1977 and 2001, the studios hosted artists including Joy Division, The Stone Roses, Happy Mondays, Inspiral Carpets, Autechre and A Certain Ratio. Middleton band K-Estate’s version of Gang of Four’s Damaged Goods received airplay on BBC Radio 6 Music and was named Track of the Day on Radio X. Organisers said tracks also featured on XS Manchester, Mersey Radio and Phoenix FM, among other stations. Listening parties took place at Rough Trade shops in London, Liverpool, Bristol and Nottingham, with vinyl copies distributed to record shops nationwide.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The man at the centre of a murder investigation in Rochdale has been named locally as John McGarry. Police were called to a report of a 'concern for welfare' of a man at a property on Curzon Road in Kirkholt shortly before 8pm on Wednesday (October 7). Emergency services attended. A man in his 50s was pronounced dead at the scene. His next of kin have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers, Greater Manchester Police said. The man has now named locally as John McGarry. He is understood to have been 56, a father and a Rochdale AFC supporter. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter A man in his 40s has been arrested on suspicion of his murder and is currently in custody for questioning. GMP said detectives were working 'at a pace' and that they are 'keeping an open mind' and 'exploring all lines of enquiry' in order to 'establish the full circumstances' surrounding Mr McGarry's death. Tributes are being paid to Mr McGarry on social media. One woman said: "So gutted fly high mate." Another said: "So sad r.i.p John." A third said: "What a horror condolences to the Mcgarry family x" A man said: "One my good friends r.ip pal up the dale shocked" Whilst another said: "Sad news fly high John." A man who said he had known Mr McGarry for over 40 years described him as a 'gentle giant'. He said: "He was a gentle giant, he was a tall lad. We used to go school with him, he was a really, really nice gentleman. "We've grown up around here, everyone knew him and we've been talking about how shocked we are. It's a sad thing." A young mum described the moment cops arrived on Curzon Road. She said: "There was a lot of police cars, ambulance and CIDs. Forensics were going in and out of the house, as well. "They were taking things out of the house. There's been all sorts going on for weeks." In a statement, Detective Superintendent Richard Hunt from GMP said: "Firstly, our thoughts remain with the family of the man who sadly died, and we have officers assigned to support them through this difficult time. "An investigation is underway and officers are working at pace to establish the circumstances which led to this man’s death. "We currently have a man in custody for questioning and ask the public to refrain from speculating at this time. This is a live investigation, and we are currently exploring all avenues of enquiry and keeping an open mind. "A scene will remain in place for several days. You may also notice an increased presence of officers in the area to provide reassurance. Please feel free to chat to them if you have any concerns. "Anyone with information regarding this incident is urged to get in touch with police on 101 and quote log 3344 of 07/10/2026, or you can make a report via the LiveChat function at gmp.police.uk Alternatively contact Crimestoppers, anonymously, on 0800 555 111.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A deaf engineer from Rochdale has developed a working prototype that captions phone conversations in real time, with support from a University of Salford programme. David Butler began researching technology to help people with hearing loss after losing his own hearing in 2017. Difficulty using the telephone was one of the communication barriers he wanted to address. The university’s BUILD AI programme helped him bring together years of research and development into E.ai.R, a prototype ready for user testing and further development. David said: “I've gone from having all the pieces of the puzzle to having something we can put into the hands of real people, test and develop, and which could ultimately help millions of people facing the same communication barriers that I've experienced myself.” BUILD AI was developed by the university’s Centre for Sustainable Innovation and delivered with NoCodeLab.ai. The six-week programme combined practical AI development with mentoring and support to explore how participants’ ideas could become products and businesses. The university said its 12 participants had brought four products to launch or near-launch, put six working prototypes into testing and developed two existing technology ventures.

candidates.source_title: This £2.50 bus ride is the best thing to cross the Pennines since Eric Cantona
candidates.source_summary: From the top deck of the 590 you can take a trip through Greater Manchester's rich industrial heritage while taking in some of the the region's most dramatic scenery
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Eric Cantona, the M62 and the Industrial Revolution. Despite the long animosity between Lancashire and Yorkshire a few things have successfully made the journey across the Pennines. And to that list you can add the 590 bus . The Rochdale to Halifax service swaps the Roch Valley for the Calder Valley as it crosses over from Greater Manchester into West Yorkshire. And along the way it takes in two marvels of the Industrial Revolution and plenty of the region's most dramatic scenery. I caught the 590 this week as far as Hebden Bridge as part of our occasional series on Greater Manchester's most scenic bus routes . Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The first thing to note is because this is a privately-owned First Bus and not a publicly-controlled Bee Network service a single ticket is £2.50 not two quid. Having stumped up the extra 10 bob, I head upstairs to join a handful of students heading home after lectures on the top deck. From Rochdale bus station it heads east out of the town centre through Smallbridge and Littleborough before crossing the border at Summit into the towns of Walsden, Todmorden and Hebden Bridge. It's a pretty unremarkable start to the journey, but soon the chicken shops and rows of brick terraces start to give way to old weavers cottages and Rochdale's famous flagstone fences. Up ahead the dramatic gritstone ridge of Blackstone Edge, marking the border between Greater Manchester and West Yorkshire, looms on the horizon. At Littleborough the bus turns north and as we begin the head into the hills we pass the former studio of the late Walter Kershaw. The painter was dubbed the 'Original Banksy' for his huge street murals and through the dusty bay window a number of his canvases can be seen still hung on the wall. At the crest of the hill, at the aptly-named village of Summit, we pass the mouth of the Summit Tunnel, a George Stephenson-designed miracle of Victorian engineering. When it opened in 1841, providing a direct link between the industrial powerhouses of Manchester and Leeds, it was the longest railway tunnel in the world. In 1984 it was also the scene of one of the biggest underground fires in transport history when a train carrying a million litres of petrol derailed. As temperatures inside reached a staggering 1,500C it took firefighters four days to extinguish the blaze. And it’s not the only reminder of our ancestors’ ingenuity along the route. To the right the Rochdale Canal, which opened 37 years before the tunnel, follows the same path along the valley. In years gone by hundreds of barges would have transported cotton, wool, coal and timber between Lancashire and Yorkshire. Today you’re much more likely to see a few pleasure cruisers eking out the last of the summer or, as I did near Walsden, a group of kayakers going for a paddle. As we approach the border with Yorkshire we also get a glimpse of a herd of alpacas, a long way from their native South America, grazing in a field of the far bank of the canal. Rochdale Council has received an application for the Burger Box, at the former Haibat Sultan restaurant at 26 Milkstone Road, to stay open until 3am daily. The council’s Licensing Sub-Committee will meet on Monday, October 12, to determine the application which names Kashif Hazarbuz as the premises licence holder. The Burger Box is described as a fast-food restaurant in a ground-floor retail unit with residential accommodation above, situated on a busy main road. Planning permission has been granted for eat-in, collection and delivery service from 11am to 11pm Monday to Sunday, and 11am to 10pm on Sundays and bank holidays. The licensing application looks to extend this to 3am each day. Under the terms of the premises licence, no alcohol can be taken into or be consumed in the restaurant at any time. Among the objections, Mrs S Rana believes that that there will be an increase in anti-social behaviour and noise from the restaurant. She is also concerned that there will be an increase in traffic and pollution if the licence is granted until 3am. Mr I Hussain believes the premises may attract anti-social behaviour within the area and lead to an increase of crime and disorder. He has concerns that the premises will create a public nuisance to residents especially with the late-night hours. He believes the licence should end at 11pm.

candidates.source_title: 'Rochdale's Chernobyl' set for clean-up in major redevelopment milestone
candidates.source_summary: A notorious former asbestos factory known as 'Rochdale's Chernobyl' is a step closer to redevelopment after landowners appointed a specialist clean-up contractor.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: 'Rochdale's Chernobyl' is a step closer to redevelopment after landowners appointed a specialist contractor to clean up the notorious former asbestos factory site. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale. It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long-held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Many locals would like to see the site transformed into a park that blends with the surrounding greenery. But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement is the appointment of a specialist contractor to carry out remediation work on the site. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Saturday saw Saints make the trip to Rochdale Rugby Club, perched on the edge of the Pennines, for their second game of the season. A fine, bright, warm day and a good pitch greeted the visitors. Injuries continue to affect Saints early in the campaign, with another three regular starters unavailable, although it was a welcome boost to see Oscar Crow and Niall Grant return on the bench. Saints made the early running, but Rochdale’s determined scrambling defence held firm until winger Sam Cotgrave barged his way over in the corner. Smith added the conversion while on kicking duties for the day. Rochdale then began to grow into the game, and with Smith shown a yellow card, the hosts took advantage. A well-worked try following missed tackles in the centre was converted to level the scores at 7-7. Rochdale missed several further scoring opportunities through dropped balls and a forward pass before eventually finding space to score beneath the posts, with the conversion giving them a 14-7 lead in front of a vocal home crowd. Saints responded well. After a penalty was kicked to touch six metres out, the resulting drive towards the line saw Joe Sanders cross for a try, with Ben Jones converting to make it 14-14. Saints continued to apply pressure, but Rochdale resisted until Olly Dodd sidestepped his defender and crossed on the stroke of half-time. Smith added the conversion on his return from the sin bin to give Saints a 21-14 lead at the break. Saints started the second half strongly, but a forced pass was spilled and Rochdale pounced, racing over in the corner. The conversion was missed, reducing the deficit to 21-19. The visitors quickly regained control. Changes in personnel helped Saints gain the upper hand in the scrum, which was beginning to take its toll on the Rochdale pack. After another attack close to the line, prop John Whittaker was driven over for a converted try, extending the lead to 28-19 and securing a bonus point. Saints were beginning to dominate possession, although Rochdale’s defence remained stubborn. A powerful scrum drive 10 metres out allowed Kincart to find Cotgrave, who slipped around his defender to score his second try of the afternoon. The conversion made it 35-19. Rochdale continued to throw everything into the contest. They were held up over the line before taking a quick tap penalty from an earlier offside offence, catching the Saints defence napping to score. The conversion was missed, but the hosts earned a deserved bonus point as the score moved to 35-24. Saints had the final say. Captain Will Grebe powered towards the line and, despite being tackled, somehow stretched out to ground the ball and score. The conversion was missed, but it completed a 40-24 victory for the visitors. It was not Saints’ best performance and they have yet to field a full-strength squad this season, but an away win and five league points represented a productive afternoon. Next up is a trip to Vale of Lune, with a 3pm kick-off. JR Planning Consultants has applied to Rochdale Council to turn the Subway store at 16 Middleton Gardens into an adult gaming centre. It follows an application it submitted in July to turn the premises into a nail bar. That application has since been withdrawn. In the latest application, JR Planning said the Planning Inspectorate appeal which allowed Jeffries Casino to occupy the former Virgin Money premises at 20 Middleton Gardens had set a precedent for the change of use in a retail area. It said: “The Inspector found that the proposed adult gaming centre was likely to generate greater footfall over a typical day than many potential Class E uses. “The Inspector also found that the use would provide opportunities for linked trips to shops, pubs and other town centre businesses and make a modest contribution to the functioning of the centre. “It was concluded that the adult gaming centre would form part of a suitable mix of uses complementary to the retail role of Middleton town centre. Therefore, the vitality and viability of the centre would not be undermined. “The Inspector also considered the potential concentration of adult gaming centres. It was concluded that the establishment of an additional non-retail unit would not be materially harmful to the vitality and viability of the town centre.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Swindon Town are bracing themselves for fitness reports on three more players following their 1-0 defeat at Rochdale . Ian Holloway’s squad was down to the bare bones at the Crown Oil Arena, as Cian Hayes’ late header denied them a first away point since the opening day of the season . Swindon switched formation for the game to make a team around the available players, and there was not much help on the bench, with only James Debayo fully fit, and this was shown in the use of substitutions , as Town did not make a tactical switch until second-half stoppage time. Ollie Clarke was not initially meant to be in the squad, but he powered through a niggle and came on for Tom Nichols, who had gone down with a knock with around 25 minutes to play. Joseph Hungbo also had to be convinced to travel with the squad, as he was dealing with discomfort in his knee, but Holloway explained to him that he couldn’t lose anyone else, and so he played the final six minutes. But the possible casualties could have serious consequences for Swindon, as, along with Nichols, Aaron Drinan went down off the ball and was stretching out his hamstring before eventually being replaced, and Jack Thomson was also struggling with a cramp before he was replaced. Thomson and Drinan have been two of the players Town have relied on during this period, as both have played 90 minutes consistently. Who showed promise and who won the real duel? Revellers young and old made the most of the entertainment in the town centre over the two-day festival, with more than 1,500 entering the Oktoberfest marquee in Middleton Gardens yesterday. Hosted by Rochdale Development Agency, Rochdale Council, the Britannia Inn, Middleton Township and and Middleton Co-operating, the entertainment kicked off yesterday with Middleton Popstars Academy, followed by the Conker Championships. This was followed by musical entertainment and fun from Big Swingy Thing and acoustic guitarist and singer Ben Floyd. The evening’s entertainment kicked off with psychedelic rock band Innafield, followed by talented local band Lazarus. Today’s festivities began with traditional oompah tunes from the Parpundales — AKA Middleton Band — to get people in the Oktoberfest mood from 1pm.
